incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High mem + tail latency on service renderer-prod (kv-prefix cache growth). auto-escalation to SRE oncall @ryan (sev2). Trace id: d9f3a2
ryan (oncall): grabbing. initial symptoms? any customer-impact reports?
megan (sre): seeing prefix_cache.object_count spike from ~120k -> 1.3M over 12m. Mem on gpu-node-7 hit 94% then OOM kill on batch-worker-3. continuous-batcher cw latency p95 jumped 4x. link to grafana: https://grafana.redwood/services/renderer-prod/dashboards/kv-prefix
lucas (support): CS ticket #4892 opened 10m ago, customer reported slow responses and occasional 502s. small subset (~1.2% of total requests) but heavy tail.
ryan (oncall): ok. runbook step 1: disable continuous batching for renderer-prod, step 2: limit batch size. Can someone flip batch config?
boris (eng): on it. reducing BATCH_MAX from 64 -> 8 via config service. command: ```curl -XPOST https://config.redwood/api/v1/services/renderer-prod -d '{"BATCH_MAX":8}'``` deploy-bot: deploying config change to renderer-prod (canary->all)
deploy-bot: canary passed (10m), promoting to 100%
megan (sre): batch reduction deployed. immediate p95 dropped ~30%, mem pressure stabilizing but prefix cache still growing. need root cause of keys explosion.
jia (sre): looking at prefix hash distribution. noticed a huge number of unique prefix keys tied to newly deployed prompt templating change from last night. hashes look like `prefix_v3:{sha256(tokenized_prefix)}` lots of variants. suspect tokenizer change + template drift.
ryan (oncall): when was tokenizer pushed?
boris (eng): tokenizer microservice was rolled at 3167860000 (yesterday). change log: switched to new bpe variant to fix rare token merging. PR #2543. Also template interpolation added optional user metadata in prompt by default (was supposed to be gated).
megan (sre): that explains the keyspace explosion: small template tweak + tokenizer producing different token sequences -> prefix hash changes -> cache misses -> continuous batching generates new entries -> exponential growth.
lucas (support): customer impact summary for CS: customers on high-throughput plans saw 10-30% higher tail latency and 0.6% increased error rate between 15:10-16:00 UTC. most recover after batch reduction but two customers had sustained issues.
amy (cs): adding notes to tickets, offering credits. we need clear RCA wording.
ryan (oncall): immediate mitigation checklist: 1) revert prompt template change (boris) 2) if revert not possible, disable prefix cache writes (toggle) 3) run cache scrub for suspect keys older than cutoff 3167869000 4) follow-up: pin tokenizer version in rollout gating.
boris (eng): revert PR #2571 (template change) in progress. pushing rollback to staging now.```git revert origin/main~2 -m 1```
deploy-bot: rollback to prior template pushed to canary (5% traffic)
deploy-bot: canary shows reduced unique prefix keys, promoting to all
megan (sre): after rollback, prefix key growth rate flattened within 10m. running scrub script to reclaim memory and remove orphaned cache entries: ```python tools/scrub_prefix_keys.py --service renderer-prod --age-cutoff 3167869000 --dry-run``` then without dry-run. scrub removed ~920k keys, reclaimed ~28GB heap.
ryan (oncall): good. now perform config toggle to stop accepting new prefix writes until we validate tokenizer alignment. command: ```curl -XPOST https://config.redwood/api/v1/services/renderer-prod -d '{"PREFIX_CACHE_WRITE":false}'```
megan (sre): toggled write=false. reads still served from cache for existing keys. also set continuous-batcher back to BATCH_MAX=16 as intermediate.
lucas (support): updated affected customers. two customers require dedicated follow-up (high cost spike). logged to CS queue.
jia (sre): collecting logs for RCA. curious edge-case: hash granularity included whitespace sanitized by old tokenizer, new tokenizer kept some control chars. that produced distinct tokenization for same visible string. attaching sample diffs:
```
old_tokens: [507, 12, 33, 9]
new_tokens: [507, 12, 33, 9, 1023]
prefix_hash_old: e3b0c442...
prefix_hash_new: 0f7a3d91...
```
boris (eng): yep found the bug in tokenizer v2.1: it no longer strips U+200B zero-width spaces in a particular path. small invisible char led to new hashes. patching tokenizer now (PR #2599) and will release as hotfix pinned to renderer-prod.
ryan (oncall): action items created: INC-12472 (hotfix tokenizer v2.1.1), INC-12473 (pin tokenizer version + add rollout gate), INC-12474 (improve cache metrics alerting threshold), and follow-up postmortem. assign owners: boris -> INC-12472, jia -> INC-12473, megan -> INC-12474.
deploy-bot: tokenizer hotfix canary passed, promoting to renderer-prod with pinned version 2.1.1
megan (sre): after hotfix, observed prefix key churn dropped to baseline, mem stable, p95 back to normal. scrub completed earlier reclaimed space.
amy (cs): estimated customer impact: ~1.2% of requests affected, tail latency increase 20-40% for affected traffic window, two customers had sustained >10% SLA breach for ~45 minutes. offering credits per policy.
ryan (oncall): handing off monitoring and follow-up to jia for the next oncall shift. I've documented mitigation steps in the incident runbook and tagged incident ticket INC-12471.
jia (sre): taking over. will coordinate postmortem and timeline. next steps: add tokenizer integration tests, add alert for anomaly in unique prefix key growth (threshold 250k/min), and add canary check for template changes.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated at 3167893500. status -> mitigated. follow-up ticket: INC-12471. SLA impact: partial (two customers, credits being processed).
ryan (oncall): closing active pager. final note: be careful with text-processing rollouts. invisible chars are tiny but dangerous. :facepalm:
megan (sre): +1. also propose adding a quick preflight that computes expected prefix-key delta before template changes go to prod.
deploy-bot: deployment history: https://deploys.redwood/renderer-prod?range=last_24h
incident-bot: resolved at 3167893900. postmortem owner: jia. retrospective meeting scheduled tomorrow 17:00 UTC in #incidents-postmortem.
